problem: Generated Rust crate required cargo fmt before validation.
observed_failure_or_friction: The starter pack compiled under cargo check, but cargo fmt --check failed on generated formatting before the first verified build.
fix_or_workaround: Run cargo fmt immediately after installing generated Rust overlays, then re-run fmt --check before expanding scope.
reusable_pattern: Treat cargo fmt --check as a first-pass generated-code quality gate for every Rust overlay.

problem: Python needs a structured boundary around Rust subprocess execution.
observed_failure_or_friction: A standalone script can run Cargo, but DAD agents need a package-level bridge that can be mocked, returns exact command data, and surfaces missing Cargo clearly.
fix_or_workaround: Add digital_asset_directory.rust_bridge.dad_scan_core with a dataclass result and CLI command that prints structured JSON.
reusable_pattern: Every target repo Rust leaf tool should have a thin, testable Python bridge before orchestration code depends on it.

problem: Scanner output paths can accidentally live inside the scanned source tree.
observed_failure_or_friction: DAD commonly writes raw and processed outputs inside the repo, but scanning the repo root and writing into that same tree can create recursive or self-observing evidence.
fix_or_workaround: The Rust scanner rejects output paths inside the scanned source until a governed safe-output policy exists; CLI callers should scan subtrees or write outside source.
reusable_pattern: Rust leaf scanners should fail closed on self-observing output layouts by default.

problem: Root-level default excludes were brittle when expressed only as glob patterns.
observed_failure_or_friction: Glob-only defaults such as **/target/** did not safely capture all root-level repo-noise directories across scanner contexts, risking .git, target, __pycache__, and similar folders entering observations.
fix_or_workaround: Match known noise directory names by path segment before glob matcher fallback, prune excluded directories, and keep regression coverage for root-level .git, target, and __pycache__ paths.
reusable_pattern: Scanner defaults should combine explicit root-level patterns, recursive patterns, and segment-based directory checks for known repo-noise names.
applies_when: A scanner has default excludes for repository noise or build/cache directories.
does_not_apply_when: The source traversal layer already has proven pathspec/gitignore-compatible directory pruning with root and nested fixtures.
danger_if_misapplied: Over-broad segment excludes can hide legitimate source directories named like cache/build folders; keep the segment list small, named, and regression-tested.

problem: Invalid glob validation and other rejected scan inputs must not create output directories as a side effect.
observed_failure_or_friction: An invalid user exclude glob can fail before scanning, but if output parents are created first the command still mutates the filesystem on a rejected invocation. The same no-write rule also matters for unsafe aliases, duplicate output paths, and zero max-file caps.
fix_or_workaround: Compile all default and user exclude globs and validate aliases, caps, and output paths before creating output parents or writing reports; assert the output directory remains absent on rejected inputs.
reusable_pattern: Scanner CLIs should validate all user-controlled patterns and output arguments before any mkdir or write side effect.
applies_when: A CLI accepts user glob/path patterns and writes generated reports, JSONL, summaries, or quarantine files.
does_not_apply_when: The command is explicitly documented as a setup command whose purpose is to create directories before validation.
danger_if_misapplied: Treating every mkdir as forbidden can block legitimate setup flows; this rule is for scan/observe commands that promise no mutation on rejected inputs.

problem: A scanner can create sensitive fingerprints even when it never copies file contents.
observed_failure_or_friction: Default Rust scanner excludes covered common build/cache folders but initially did not skip DAD mail/control/evidence surfaces or common credential files, so small private files could receive content_sha256 observations by default.
fix_or_workaround: Prune DAD repo-local control/evidence directories such as .digital-asset, raw, processed, state, and audit, and skip credential-like files including .env, .netrc, .npmrc, .pypirc, SSH private key names, and common key/certificate extensions before hashing.
reusable_pattern: Scanner defaults should treat secret-bearing files and DAD private evidence/control surfaces as quarantine-only unless a reviewed policy explicitly opts into scanning them.
applies_when: A scanner emits metadata or hashes for local files and may run against DAD, enrolled repos, or repos containing mailbox/evidence/control-plane surfaces.
does_not_apply_when: A scanner is operating under an explicit reviewed secret-scanning policy that permits credential fingerprinting and stores results in a protected sink.
danger_if_misapplied: Over-broad default excludes can hide legitimate source assets named raw, processed, state, or audit; keep DAD-specific top-level directory exclusions documented and regression-tested.

applies_when: A raw source package is a repository/archive with both corpus text and non-text or duplicate support artifacts.
danger_if_misapplied: A filter can accidentally exclude legitimate canonical text or select a duplicate/wrong edition; require exact expected book counts, per-source path rules, hashes, and review before downstream use.
does_not_apply_when: The raw artifact is already a single governed source text file with no bundled extras and a manifest proves that shape.
fix_or_workaround: Keep raw archives immutable and build a separate canonical-only candidate source view with inclusion/exclusion ledgers. Future source-language processing must consume the filtered source view, not raw archives directly.
observed_failure_or_friction: T431 raw archives for UXLC, OSHB, SBLGNT, UGNT, and CNTR-SR included extra material. Direct downstream ingestion from raw archives risks contaminating canonical Bible processing with documentation, application artifacts, duplicate text formats, or source variants.
problem: Downloaded source archives can contain canonical Bible text plus docs, code, images, nested archives, duplicate renderings, metadata, and non-selected variants.
reusable_pattern: For public corpus intake, split source package download from deterministic canonical-file filtering; validate inclusion counts and exclusion ledgers before tokenization. This is a strong Rust leaf-tool candidate once schemas stabilize: scan zip -> classify paths -> hash/copy selected files -> emit JSONL/YAML -> Python orchestrates.

problem: Generated canonical refresh commands can accidentally import apocrypha/deuterocanonical books from a raw package that contains more than the canonical 66.
observed_failure_or_friction: During T431 validation, running pipelines/ingest/usfm_importer.py without --canonical-66-filter generated 38,058 passage records and included books such as Tobit and 1 Esdras in ignored canonical outputs, causing canonical-66 validation and baseline hash gates to fail.
fix_or_workaround: For merge/validation refreshes, run python pipelines/ingest/usfm_importer.py --canonical-66-filter before validate_all.py. Treat any unfiltered generated canonical output as environment noise to discard/regenerate, not as source truth.
reusable_pattern: Any corpus importer that reads a raw archive with canonical plus appendix/deuterocanonical/support material needs an explicit scope flag or config profile at generation time, and validators should fail closed when generated canonical outputs include out-of-scope books.
applies_when: A raw Bible/source package includes canonical books plus appendix, deuterocanonical, front matter, glossary, or support material.
A generated canonical layer is refreshed for validation gates.
does_not_apply_when: The command intentionally generates a separate noncanonical/appendix candidate layer with a different trust zone and output root.
danger_if_misapplied: Blindly forcing canonical-66 filtering can erase intentionally separate appendix/deuterocanonical evidence layers. The rule is for canonical output roots and validation refreshes, not for catalog-only or candidate comparative evidence lanes.
evidence_refs: logos-scripture-graph:scripts/validate_all.py failure then pass after filtered regenerate

problem: Local validation can miss commit-diff watched-path gates when the validator compares origin/main...HEAD and the remediation is still uncommitted.
observed_failure_or_friction: PR #134 failed GitHub validate because docs/roadmap changes required chunking_theological_decision_register updates. Local validate_all had passed before the register/lesson update because the exact base-ref watched-path gate was not run against the final committed diff.
fix_or_workaround: For PRs that touch watched governance/roadmap paths, run the relevant validator with --base-ref origin/main after committing the remediation, not only before commit. Treat uncommitted working-tree validation as insufficient for diff gates.
reusable_pattern: CI parity prompts should include a post-commit base-ref gate pass for validators that inspect git diff, especially decision-register, lesson-index, task-scope, and changed-path policy gates.
applies_when: A validator uses git merge-base/diff to require companion ledger or policy updates.
A PR touches watched paths under docs/roadmap, control planes, task scope, registries, or policy files.
does_not_apply_when: The validator only inspects file contents and does not inspect committed diff state.
danger_if_misapplied: Running only base-ref gates without ordinary content validators can miss malformed files; use both content validation and committed-diff validation.

problem: A canonical source view can drift from its immutable raw archive if validation only checks the view file against its own ledger row.
observed_failure_or_friction: A review found that T431 check mode proved ledger coverage and candidate-view checksum consistency, but did not rehash the selected ZIP member bytes. A future edit could mutate data/candidate/original_language_evidence/canonical_source_views files and update included_files.jsonl, leaving downstream T432+ to consume corrupted evidence while CI passed.
fix_or_workaround: In check mode, re-open the raw archive, read every included source_archive_path, and require the archive member bytes, ledger sha256, ledger size_bytes, and committed view file bytes to match exactly. Also shape-lock the raw tree to source_manifest.yaml, raw/<declared archive>, and catalog-only witness YAML so overlay-like files cannot evade by avoiding magic filenames.
reusable_pattern: For any derived source-view or filtered-corpus layer, validators must prove both internal ledger consistency and byte-for-byte lineage back to immutable raw inputs before downstream agents are told to consume the derived view.
applies_when: A task creates canonical-only or filtered source views from raw archives.
Downstream tasks consume derived candidate files rather than raw archives directly.
The raw package includes extra docs, metadata, duplicate formats, variants, or noncanonical material.
does_not_apply_when: The derived view is intentionally human-edited and has a separate reviewed promotion policy with explicit provenance rows.
The raw input is a database/API where byte-for-byte archive-member proof is impossible and an equivalent immutable snapshot/hash proof exists.
danger_if_misapplied: Blind byte equality can block legitimate normalization, decompression, or transcoding pipelines; in those cases require an explicit transform manifest and fixture-level source-to-output proof instead of raw byte equality.

problem: A Rust fast path can weaken the Python gate it replaces if parity testing only covers happy-path or string-presence behavior.
observed_failure_or_friction: A review found that T424's Rust JSONL validator rejected missing canon_profiles but not falsey empty/null values, and skipped TranslationWitness referential checking when passage_id was absent. Python failed those cases. The canonical-scope wrapper also exposed custom --canon while Python fallback/compare used only the repo default canon config.
fix_or_workaround: Make Rust match Python truthiness for --require-canon, check every TranslationWitness for missing or unknown passage_id, reject custom --canon when Python fallback/compare is requested, and add negative parity fixtures for empty/null canon_profiles, missing passage_id, unknown passage_id, custom-canon compare rejection, and validate_all gate shape.
reusable_pattern: Before enabling Rust acceleration in a Python-governed validation pipeline, prove negative-case semantic parity against the Python validator and keep Python as the governance orchestrator. Fast paths should fail closed, compare against Python during rollout, and narrow unsupported fallback arguments instead of pretending parity exists.
applies_when: A Rust CLI is introduced to accelerate an existing Python validator.
validate_all or CI will call the Rust path by default when available.
The Python validator uses truthiness, referential integrity, custom config, or other semantics not captured by simple schema checks.
does_not_apply_when: Rust is the original authoritative implementation and Python is only a thin launcher with no independent semantics.
The Rust path is shadow-only and cannot affect CI verdicts or merge gates.
danger_if_misapplied: Over-demanding full parity can delay useful Rust scaffolds; apply this rule before Rust becomes verdict-authoritative, not to read-only performance experiments clearly marked shadow-only.

problem: Manifest-level source metadata can be broader than the selected canonical source-view file or span.
observed_failure_or_friction: T433 review found UGNT was package-level metadata-rich, but the selected Philemon canonical source view exposed plain Greek USFM without visible per-token Strong's or morphology fields. If a downstream pilot trusted package-level flags directly, it could populate Strong's or morphology rows without span-local evidence.
fix_or_workaround: Require row builders and validators to prove metadata availability at the selected canonical source-view file and target span before populating Strong's, morphology, lemma, witness, or variant fields. For the first pilot, use SBLGNT source tokens and keep WEB Strong's only as translation-side hints.
reusable_pattern: Evidence pipelines should separate package/manifest capability flags from row-level observed fields. Treat broad metadata flags as routing hints, then require span-local parser proof before creating evidence rows. This is a good future Rust scanner rule after Python pilots prove row shapes.
applies_when: A source package advertises metadata such as Strong's, morphology, lemmas, variants, witnesses, or editorial layers.
A task builds row-level evidence from a filtered/canonical source view rather than the raw archive.
A future Rust scanner will populate evidence ledgers from heterogeneous source packages.
does_not_apply_when: The selected source-view file/span visibly contains the field and the parser records exact source markers, offsets, hashes, and confidence.
The row is intentionally catalog-level metadata and clearly does not claim span-local token evidence.
danger_if_misapplied: Over-requiring span-local proof for intentionally catalog-level rows can block useful source-catalog planning. Apply this rule to token/span evidence population, not to clearly labeled catalog-only research.

problem: A fast Rust scanner can look authoritative unless its output root, text policy, and parity target are constrained before agents consume it.
observed_failure_or_friction: T435 added a Rust SBLGNT XML scanner that can observe 27 NT source-view files quickly, but the safe design required no-text build-only ledgers, Python authority validation, and T433 Phlm.1.1-3 shadow parity before any production candidate roots opened. Without those constraints, future agents could treat token order, punctuation/sigla, token hashes, or Rust speed as source-language truth, alignment truth, source-tradition preference, or theology authority.
fix_or_workaround: Keep Rust in a deterministic leaf role: consume canonical source views, emit ignored build ledgers with counts/hashes/lineage only, require --no-authority and --no-text, validate all authority flags in Python, and compare one reviewed pilot span before trusting the scanner as substrate evidence. Defer broader Hebrew/metadata-rich sources until a separate pilot proves those assumptions.
reusable_pattern: For corpus evidence scanners, pair Rust observation with a Python governance validator and a same-scope shadow parity fixture from a prior reviewed pilot. Generated Rust ledgers should stay build-only until a later task explicitly opens production candidate roots.
applies_when: A Rust scanner is introduced after a small Python pilot proves row semantics.
The scanner observes source text, tokens, editorial markers, or corpus metadata that could be mistaken for authority.
Generated ledgers are intended to feed future AI agents or downstream validators.
does_not_apply_when: Rust is only running a local benchmark with no persisted ledgers and no downstream consumers.
A production root has already been explicitly opened by a reviewed owner-gated task with separate authority policy.
danger_if_misapplied: Requiring a prior pilot for every tiny scanner can slow harmless tooling; apply this rule when scanner outputs can influence evidence rows, alignment, corpus trust, or future agent decisions.

problem: Metadata-rich source XML fields can be mistaken for local schema authority, and a Rust scanner would scale that mistake quickly if source-specific parser semantics are not proven first.
observed_failure_or_friction: The OSHB Jonah canonical source view exposes w@lemma attributes on 688 words while the T431 canonical source-view manifest says contains_source_provided_lemmas=false. UXLC and OSHB have matching Jonah verse/token counts, but their XML structures and metadata semantics differ. A generalized scanner could wrongly copy OSHB lemma attributes into Strong's, lemma, lexeme, morphology, or translation-faithfulness rows.
fix_or_workaround: Before Rust expansion, run a Python no-text observation/parity pilot that consumes only canonical source views, records source-view file/verse/token-shape/editorial-shape ledgers with counts and hashes, detects manifest/source XML metadata drift, and keeps production roots closed. Block Rust expansion until drift is fixed or explicitly policy-covered and source-specific UXLC/OSHB parser expectations exist.
reusable_pattern: For heterogeneous corpus sources, validate metadata semantics before performance scaling: parity on counts is necessary but not sufficient. No-text ledgers should prove source shape, lineage, field presence, and authority limits without storing text or low-entropy metadata values. Rust should implement only the parser contracts already proven by Python fixtures and negative tests.
applies_when: A source package exposes fields named like local schema fields, such as lemma, morph, Strong, witness, or variant.
Multiple source views for the same corpus have matching refs/counts but different metadata semantics.
A future Rust scanner would consume heterogeneous XML formats or metadata-rich source views.
does_not_apply_when: The task is catalog-only and does not create token/span evidence rows.
The source-specific parser contract and metadata policy are already reviewed, fixture-covered, and authority-bounded.
danger_if_misapplied: Blocking Rust after every harmless metadata mismatch can delay useful scanners; apply this lesson when metadata fields could feed source-language, lexical, alignment, witness, variant, translation, chunking, KG, retrieval, or theology surfaces.

problem: A source field name such as lemma can look semantically equivalent to a local schema field even when the source declares a different meaning, causing AI agents or Rust scanners to promote metadata into false authority.
observed_failure_or_friction: OSHB XML uses w@lemma attributes and an OSIS workPrefix declaration mapping //w/@lemma to Strong. Treating that field as local lemma authority would have opened lemma, Strong's, lexical, translation-faithfulness, or theology surfaces from a field-name match instead of a reviewed source-specific parser contract.
fix_or_workaround: Add explicit policy-cover fields that separate source attribute presence from local evidence-row authority: contains_source_provided_lemma_attributes=true, contains_source_provided_strong_lookup_hints=true, contains_source_provided_lemmas=false, contains_source_provided_strongs=false, lemma_attribute_interpretation=strong_lookup_hint, and lemma_attribute_authority=metadata_only_not_local_lemma_or_strong_authority. Keep Rust expansion blocked until parser contracts and no-text parity prove the semantics.
reusable_pattern: When ingesting heterogeneous corpora, require semantic policy-cover for source attributes whose names overlap local schema authority fields. Fast scanners should consume policy-covered contracts, not infer meaning from XML/JSON key names. Validators should check both key presence and declared source semantics before scaling ingestion.
applies_when: A raw source exposes fields named lemma, morph, strong, witness, variant, speaker, red-letter, canon, authority, or similar high-impact schema names.
A field may be a lookup hint, index code, editorial marker, or source-specific convention rather than the repo's local evidence type.
A Rust or other accelerated scanner would otherwise scale key-name assumptions across a corpus.
does_not_apply_when: A reviewed parser contract proves the source field exactly matches the local schema field and validators cover negative examples.
The row is clearly catalog-only and cannot feed token/span evidence, alignment, witness, variant, translation, KG, retrieval, chunking, or theology surfaces.
danger_if_misapplied: Over-separating every harmless field name can create noisy policy files. Apply this to fields that can affect evidence authority, not to ordinary structural fields like file name or line count.
extra_context: This is the same class of problem as dirty corpus intake, where public packages include docs, extra formats, metadata, or ambiguous fields. DAD should preserve an extra_context area in future lesson/requirement packets so repos can explain why a requirement exists, not just the minimum rule.

problem: Rust original-language scanners can pass count parity while still misunderstanding source semantics, especially for overlapping authority fields like lemma, morph, strong, variant, and witness.
observed_failure_or_friction: T438 planning found that UXLC/OSHB Jonah count parity and SBLGNT Philemon parity are useful evidence, but not enough to authorize production alignment or broader Rust scanning. A scanner could match verse/token counts and still treat field names or package-level metadata as lexical authority, translation judgment, preferred reading, or theology authority.
fix_or_workaround: Separate the work into goal selection, source-specific parser contracts, Rust no-text scanner/checker parity, and owner-gated production-root opening. Require negative semantic parity fixtures before Rust scales: missing/empty/null authority fields, field-name collisions, unsupported raw-archive direct consumption, stale lineage, forbidden text leakage, and count-match/meaning-mismatch cases.
reusable_pattern: Count parity is necessary but not sufficient. For evidence corpora, Rust should scale parser contracts only after Python-governed semantic validators and negative fixtures prove what each field means. Rust emits no-text shape/count/hash/coverage evidence; Python keeps governance and authority verdicts.
applies_when: A Rust scanner will parse original-language, legal, medical, or other high-authority corpora.
Two sources have matching refs/counts but different field semantics or metadata conventions.
A downstream pipeline could treat parser output as alignment, witness, variant, translation, KG, retrieval, chunking, or theology authority.
does_not_apply_when: The Rust tool only checks low-risk file size/hash presence and cannot influence semantic rows or downstream authority.
A reviewed source-specific parser contract with negative fixtures already proves field semantics and Python parity.
danger_if_misapplied: Demanding semantic parity for every simple checksum tool can slow harmless automation. Apply this when scanner output can feed evidence rows, interpretation, ranking, promotion, or downstream AI decisions.
extra_context: This lesson supports the user's Rust-first direction while preventing Rust from becoming a high-speed authority leak. It should become part of future DAD Rust scanner requirements as an extra-context rationale, not just a minimum rule.

problem: A future Rust alignment scanner needs a full-book parity fixture, but a text-bearing fixture can accidentally become a source-text import or authority surface.
observed_failure_or_friction: T439 expanded the SBLGNT-to-WEB Philemon bridge from 3 verses to all 25 verses. The safe shape was to store source-token IDs, hashes, counts, references, WEB token IDs, and redacted editorial-layer facts without visible Greek or English text. This preserves full-book coverage while avoiding production root opening and visible text import.
fix_or_workaround: Build one small-book no-text Python pilot fixture before Rust acceleration. Validators should lock exact refs/counts, reject visible text keys, reject Strong/lemma/morphology population, reject alignment confidence upgrades, prove WEB token coverage, keep production roots empty, and then use the fixture for later Rust no-text parity.
reusable_pattern: Before adding a Rust full-book scanner for high-authority text, create a no-text Python fixture over one small book. Let Python prove semantics and authority boundaries first; then Rust can match counts, hashes, IDs, coverage joins, and negative cases at speed.
applies_when: A future Rust scanner will expand from a tiny pilot to full-book or full-corpus evidence coverage.
Visible source text storage is licensed but still governance-sensitive.
Downstream agents could mistake pilot rows for production evidence, translation judgment, or theology authority.
does_not_apply_when: The Rust tool has no persisted output and cannot influence downstream evidence rows.
A reviewed production root has already been explicitly opened with separate source-text storage policy and authority controls.
danger_if_misapplied: No-text fixtures are less useful for human linguistic review than visible-text packets. Use no-text fixtures for scanner parity and coverage; use separate owner-gated/reviewed packets when human source-language reading requires visible text.
extra_context: This supports a Rust-growing codebase without using Rust for first interpretation. Rust should inherit a proved no-text fixture, not invent corpus semantics while scaling.

problem: A future Rust scanner can scale the wrong meaning if multiple source packages expose the same book with matching refs/counts but different XML shapes and authority-bearing field names such as lemma or morph.
observed_failure_or_friction: Jonah UXLC and OSHB both expose 48 refs and 688 tokens, but UXLC is a clean no-lemma/no-morph/no-Strong source view while OSHB exposes lemma and morph attributes. The OSHB lemma attribute is policy-covered as a Strong lookup hint, not local lemma or Strong authority, and morph remains source metadata rather than local morphology-row population.
fix_or_workaround: Create a source-specific parser contract before Rust implementation. The contract records source manifests, canonical source-view manifests, included-files lineage, source-view checksums, license, XML element shapes, expected counts, attribute semantics, editorial-marker semantics, negative fixtures, production-root closure, and Rust deferral. Rust can later implement a no-text checker against the contract, not infer semantics from keys or count parity.
reusable_pattern: Before Rust scans a second source family, require a parser contract that separates coverage parity from semantic authority. Count/hash/ref agreement proves only coverage unless the source-specific field meanings and negative fixtures are reviewed.
applies_when: A Rust scanner will parse multiple editions or source packages for the same corpus.
Packages use overlapping field names such as lemma, morph, strong, witness, variant, speaker, red-letter, canon, or authority.
Count parity is tempting to treat as semantic parity.
does_not_apply_when: The Rust tool only checks raw file existence, byte size, or checksum and cannot feed semantic rows.
A reviewed source-specific parser contract and negative fixtures already prove field semantics for every consumed source.
danger_if_misapplied: Over-contracting simple checksum tools can slow harmless automation. Apply this pattern where Rust output can feed evidence rows, alignment, translation review, witness/variant work, KG/retrieval, chunking, or other high-authority decisions.
extra_context: This is the Rust-growth path the user wants: use Rust for deterministic scanner/checker leaf work after Python/control-plane semantics are explicit. DAD should treat parser contracts as reusable assets for any corpus where high-speed Rust can otherwise amplify a field-name misunderstanding.

applies_when: Multiple repos or branches are sending Rust rollout feedback or DAD mail.
DAD worktree is dirty during Rust rollout and operators need to know whether mail is corrupt.
A repo agent wants to send learning-loop feedback to DAD.
danger_if_misapplied: Treating all git dirt as mailbox corruption can block useful work; treating all duplicate outbox packets as harmless retries can hide copied worktrees, wrong-box writes, or provenance spoofing.
does_not_apply_when: The task is a single-repo local edit with no mail collection/routing/delivery.
A reviewed route/collection/delivery audit already proves the packet lifecycle and no duplicate source identity is present.
fix_or_workaround: Require source repos to write Rust feedback to their own .digital-asset/mail/outbox.jsonl, require DAD collection and route audit before central inbox/outbox rows can move forward, keep routine Rust rollout packets in ignored processed/mail/staged/rust_rollout, and treat tracked mail/outbox/rust_rollout as deliberate reference-snapshot evidence only.
observed_failure_or_friction: Mail doctor showed the mail spool clean while the git worktree was dirty with Rust rollout reference snapshots and broad DAD buildout edits. Red-team review found central routed outbox rows lacked route audit, and unknown-source duplicate outboxes could be mistaken for harmless retries.
problem: Concurrent Rust rollout feedback can make DAD look very dirty, and agents may confuse source repo outbox traffic, DAD central collection/routing, tracked Rust reference snapshots, ignored staging, and ordinary worktree dirt.
reusable_pattern: Classify dirty state before repair: mailbox corruption blocks collect/route/deliver; tracked Rust reference snapshot churn needs review/audit but is not live mail; ignored staging churn is routine generated output; ordinary worktree dirt needs normal code review. A clean Rust structural probe never replaces mail doctor with reviewed repo coverage.
